title: 30-minute Focus Logbook: Micro-OKR Sprint Notes
content:
Why this exists
- Quick, repeatable 30-min focused blocks to move small OKR tasks forward instead of long vague sessions.
- Build habit: finish one concrete output per block.

Context / top-level objective
- Personal OKR: Increase feature experiment throughput and reduce time-to-observable(rolling metrics) for latency regressions.
- Why: demo readiness for Q1 partner pilot; reduce firefighting overhead on on-call.

How I use this logbook
- Run 2–3 x 30-min blocks/day on focal tasks. Capture what I actually shipped or learned.
- If blocked, note blocker + next action. Keep friction low.

Session entries (reverse-chronological)
2026-02-14 10:00–10:30 — Block A: micro-eval harness cleanup
- Goal: get a local eval run to finish under 20m for the smoke set.
- Done: trimmed prompt fixtures (removed obsolete examples), added early exit on NaN loss.
- Outcome: full run time reduced ~18% (est). Smoke run completed locally.
- Next: push small test harness change, open PR. PR draft link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/210
- Blockers: flaky dataset loader — add a lightweight pre-validate step.

2026-02-13 16:00–16:30 — Block B: latency SLO dashboard notes
- Goal: propose one metric for request-level latency SLO (p95 of cold-starts vs warmed).
- Notes: p95 alone hides tail multiples; include p99 and 95th/50th ratio as a simple signal.
- Todo: sanity-check with last 7 days of console traces (route: api/v1/generate).
- Linked artifact: traces -> console/dashboard -> ticket JIRA-3421

2026-02-11 09:30–10:00 — Block C: batching experiment idea
- Idea: dynamic batch cap for image-to-text reranker traffic spikes. Start conservative: cap growth factor 1.5 and emergency flush after 250ms.
- Hypothesis: will reduce 95th latency by 8–12% for bursty windows, cost neutral overall.
- Experiment plan: A/B for two routes, measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost per request.

Quick weekly retro (2/7–2/14)
- Wins: shipped eval harness improvement; clarified SLO metric draft; got alignment with infra on trace retention.
- Misses: batching experiment still in design (need infra time), didn't complete PR review on runtime change.
- Patterns: mornings are best for focused novelty; afternoons for triage.

Micro-OKR checkpoints (current week)
- O1: Reduce mean time-to-detect regression from deploy -> alert by 40% (baseline: 3h).
  - Actions: add targeted smoke evals + infra trace sampling.
  - Progress: smoke evals automated locally, infra sampling convo scheduled with Oliver (Weds).
- O2: Decrease per-request cold-start token overhead by 15% for small models.
  - Actions: test KV cache warmup prefetch for common prefixes.
  - Progress: prototype in branch; perf numbers inconclusive.

Open blockers / decisions
- Do we onboard the small-run smoke eval into CI or schedule nightly on Dedicated? Tradeoff: CI run increases PR latency. Need product sign-off. (Ping: @Rae)
- Decision: initial batch flush timeout: 200ms vs 250ms? 200ms reduces latency more but may increase micro-cost. Run canary with 250ms then tighten.

Triage queue (one-line tasks for next 30-min blocks)
- Add pre-validate to eval dataset loader.
- Draft PR description for eval harness change.
- Run quick dashboard query for p95 cold-starts last 7d.
- Sketch experiments table for dynamic batch cap (metrics to collect).

Notes to self / heuristics
- Ship the smallest possible change that makes the signal observable.
- When blocked >2 blocks in a row, switch to pairing — faster unblock.
- Keep logs: one output per block (commit, PR, metric, doc).

Links & shortcuts
- Slack: #eng-serving-runtime (pin: inline traces example)
- Dashboard quick query: console://dashboard/latency/p95?route=api/v1/generate
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/search?q=kv+cache

Reflection (end of page)
- This format forces closure. Small wins compound.
- Next week: try 4 x 30-min blocks split across morning + early evening to reduce context switching.

Unresolved questions (to bring up in 1:1 with Rae)
- Cost allocation for nightly smoke runs (hosted credits vs dedicated engineer time).
- Risk tolerance for tightening batch flush in prod routes.
